title: IPC hello — the client's first frame
description: Opens an IPC v2 connection: version, client identity, an optional endpoint claim, and the capabilities being requested. The socket the client connected to is an authority-domain input the frame cannot influence — an administrative client connects to the admin socket and MUST omit the endpoint claim, and a data-socket connection can never obtain `admin.*` whatever it asks for here.

ipc_version.description: Negotiated in hello, never configured as an operator profile value. Major is 2: endpoint addressing made this a major version change (ADR-0030).

kind.description: Endpoint-binding and configuration hygiene ONLY. Not cryptographic authentication, and never the selector that grants administrative authority: a client claiming an administrative kind on the data socket stays categorically ineligible for `admin.*` (ADR-0037).

endpoint.description: Omitted by a read-only diagnostics client, and REQUIRED to be omitted on the admin socket, which never owns a lease. A direct-capable client needs a successful exclusive claim; the lease is connection-bound and cannot be changed without reconnecting.

requested_capabilities.description: Requested, not granted. The reply carries what policy actually allowed; an unknown or unauthorized request is refused rather than silently elevated.

features.description: Optional negotiated features, e.g. `keepalive`. With `ipc.keepalive.require_for_endpoint_lease` true (the default), a client claiming an endpoint without negotiating keepalive is denied `CapabilityDenied` — the lease is never granted and then revoked.
